channel.title: Responsible AI & Neurodivergence, Naba Rizvi
channel.description: Daily curated research feed on ethical and responsible AI, with emphasis on neurodivergent people and serious mental illness.

item.title: The Problem of Atypicality in LLM-Powered Psychiatry
item.description: The argument names a risk that most safety work sidesteps, namely that because these systems generate from population level statistical regularities, a response that is unremarkable for a general user can be dangerously wrong once interpreted by someone whose cognitive or interpretive patterns are atypical. The authors hold that prompt engineering and fine tuning are insufficient against a structural risk of this kind, since the problem lives in the relationship between a typical output and an atypical reader rather than in any particular bad output. Their proposal is Dynamic Contextual Certification, a staged and reversible deployment process borrowed from clinical translation, which treats interpretive safety as an ongoing obligation rather than a benchmark score to be cleared once.

item.title: Assessing Risks of Large Language Models in Mental Health Support: A Framework for Automated Clinical AI Red Teaming
item.description: A red teaming framework that pairs AI psychotherapists with simulated patient agents carrying dynamic cognitive and affective models, then scores whole session simulations against a quality of care and risk ontology rather than against isolated replies. Run across 369 sessions with six deployed systems and 15 clinically validated patient personas, it surfaces specific iatrogenic outcomes, most notably validation of patient delusions and failure to de escalate suicide risk. The authors also validated an audit dashboard with engineers, clinicians and policy experts, which is the practical contribution, since it gives non engineers a way to inspect what a therapeutic conversation actually did before deployment rather than after harm.

item.title: Large Language Models as Simulative Agents for Neurodivergent Adult Psychometric Profiles
item.description: Twenty six adults completed a 29 item open ended interview plus the ASRS, BAARS-IV, AQ and RAADS-R, and two models were asked to infer a psychological profile from the interview and then answer each instrument in role, a design aimed at the real problem that ADHD, autism and cognitive disengagement syndrome overlap enough to blunt standard instruments. Both models beat a randomized baseline, GPT-4o most reliably, and simulated responses tracked human data closely on three of the four measures. The interesting failure is local rather than global, since the AQ showed subscale specific limitations, particularly on attention to detail, which is exactly the kind of gap that would be invisible in an aggregate accuracy score and matters if synthetic participants start standing in for autistic and ADHD respondents.

item.title: Ethical decision-making for AI in mental health: the Integrated Ethical Approach for Computational Psychiatry (IEACP) framework
item.description: A framework synthesised from 83 studies that turns computational psychiatry ethics into a procedure rather than a principles list, moving through identification, analysis, decision making, implementation and review. Each stage is held to six core values, namely beneficence, autonomy, justice, privacy, transparency and scientific integrity, so a team can locate where in a project a given concern actually belongs instead of gesturing at ethics in the abstract. The case for building something psychiatry specific is that generic AI and healthcare guidance does not reach dilemmas where algorithmic bias and the erosion of clinical judgement interact with diagnoses that already carry heavy social consequences.
